english: Good-fame, our quern broke. Do you grind wheat in your millstone? Grind it in my millstone; it is old. Is wheat plentiful? Yes, little wheat this year; it did not rain. Now bring me grain/meal. You are dear to us. I will bring you honey in spring. Honey is sweet to old women.
uncertain: first line: 'gʷréh₂wō' as loc 'in the millstone' vs nom; who is speaking

english: Is your wagon at home? It stands by the wall. What do you ask? Hay lies in my field and it may rain. I want to carry it home in your wagon. Take the wagon and yoke your two oxen. The wheel is old, do not drive fast. I will not drive fast, and I will bring your hay back(?).

Grandfather, our father left a spear and a bow. Advise us. My brother and I both want the bow. Which of you is the swifter? I am the swifter, and I the bigger. Now let the swift one take the bow and the big one take the spear. Young men, you two have won. Grandfather, you advised us and (we two) rejoiced(?).

Brother, our father died. How will his cows be shared? He left ten cows and five horses. We share the cows in two, and I take five cows. Who takes the horses? As the firstborn I take three horses. Now give me the best one. You are young. I give you the best one. You are a good brother.
uncertain: 'gʷṓs dwís bʰéh₂gōwos' — 1du perf? 'we two have divided the cows in two'

english: King, we drove cows from the enemies. How many will you give me? How many enemies did you kill? I killed two of them and two of them fled. Now you will take four cows. The first cow is Perkwunos's. Did Perkwunos win for us? The enemies fled from his thunder. Now may he be honoured best(?). Young man, hero, may your fame be great.
uncertain: 'nu spéh₁istom h₂r̥yéh₁t' — 'may he fit/allot the best'?

english: Kindly one, your kettle is here. What is it, heavy? There is pig fat in it. At dinner we killed a pig. You owe me nothing; why do you bring me fat? You gave me a kettle and I give you fat. Now come to our house and eat with us. I will come with my children. She whom my husband married cooks meat.
uncertain: last line syntax: 'h₁íh₂ wédʰe pótim moy' — she led my husband (married)? relative?
